# Parallel Raises $20M in Series B Funding; Tyler Technologies Scoops Up Edulink

  

By Michelle Caffrey — December 12, 2025   2 min read

k 12dealmaking  

Getty

 Save to favorites
 Print)

Email   Facebook   LinkedIn   Twitter   Copy URL

Special education company Parallel raised $20 million in Series B funding, the company announced.

The round was led by Valspring Capital, a healthcare-focused fund founded by former Bain Capital investors, and included participation from existing investor Rethink Impact. The company has raised a total of $48.9 million in funding since it was founded in 2021, according to data from Tracxn. [...] The company was able to raise the funding, it said, in part because of recently released outcomes data indicating 98% of students using its services met or exceed their individualized education program goals during the 2024-25 school year.

“We are committed to partnering with districts, as well as the families they serve, to make a difference. The outcomes data reinforces the efficacy and impact of our services, which we look to expand even more broadly with the support of this latest round of funding,” Parallel CEO and founder Diana Heldfond said in a statement.

Tyler Techologies Scoops Up Edulink. Enterprise resource system maker Tyler Technologies acquired K-12 evaluation and workflow company Edulink Inc., the companies announced.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed. [...] With the funding, the company aims to support its national expansion efforts and advance its current proprietary clinical technology.

Parallel offers districts digital special education services provided by professionals licensed in each customers’ state including speech-language pathologists, school psychologists, school social workers, and special educators. Their goal is to provider under-staffed and under-resourced districts with the expertise they need to meet students’ special education goals. It reports serving more than 10,000 students in 25 states. Parallel aims to be active in all 50 states in the next two years.

Lehi, Utah — October 9, 2025

Early-stage startups often struggle with finance. Spreadsheets break, assumptions go untested, and fundraising decks leave investors unconvinced. For most founders, managing finance is a constant headache—critical decisions are slowed, plans are ignored, and mistakes are repeated.

Parallel is tackling that problem head-on. Today, the startup announced $2.4 million in seed funding to launch its AI-native finance platform paired with a network of dedicated fractional CFOs. The round was led by Night Capital (Austin) and K5 Tokyo Black (San Francisco), with participation from Penny Jar Capital (San Francisco), Background VC (San Francisco), Mintaka VC (Belmont, CA), and Path Ventures (Menlo Park). results.content:
Oct 9, 2025 — $2.4M Seed raised

Parallel announced a $2.4M seed round to launch its AI-native forecasting platform and a network of fractional CFOs for startups.

## Investment Summary

Frazier VC Fund IV invested in Parallel in 2023 through a primary investment, reflecting conviction in the company’s mission to bring financial clarity and forecasting discipline to startup operators. Parallel’s product direction aligns with long-term demand for scalable, software-driven infrastructure that helps teams plan runway, hiring, and fundraising decisions with confidence.

## Why We Invested [...] Deal Type: Primary

## Company Overview

Parallel is strategic finance software built for startup founders to help them make faster, more confident decisions using a financial forecast they can trust. The platform focuses on runway and burn clarity, scenario planning for hiring and spend, and generating investor-ready outputs without constantly rebuilding spreadsheet models. Parallel is designed to simplify FP&A workflows for early-stage teams and provide real-time financial clarity for planning and fundraising.

## Public Funding / Capital Events

Aug 29, 2023 — $1.85M Pre-Seed raised

Parallel announced a $1.85M pre-seed round. Public reporting lists Penny Jar Capital as a leader, with participation from Peak Capital, the Frazier VC, Convoi Ventures, and leaders from Divvy. [...] ## Why We Invested

Frazier VC invested in Parallel because we believe the company is positioned for strong growth in a large market where early-stage teams increasingly need better financial visibility and planning systems. Parallel’s platform is scalable and purpose-built for founders, replacing fragile spreadsheet workflows with intuitive forecasting, scenario planning, and investor-ready outputs. We also value the company’s differentiation in simplifying FP&A for startups and embedding itself into critical decision-making workflows, creating meaningful product stickiness over time. Finally, we prioritize strong leadership teams, and Parallel’s execution focus and operator-first approach made it a compelling investment for Fund IV.
